paragraphs: Friend, here is what I hear in this whole last chapter. Paul warns hard because he loves them. He writes these things while he's away "so that when I am present I will not need to be severe in my use of the authority that the Lord gave me for building you up, not for tearing you down" (2 Corinthians 13:10). A warning from someone who wants you built up is a gift, even when it stings like a hot pan handle.

Then Paul turns the mirror around. The Corinthians wanted proof about him, so he says, "Examine yourselves to see whether you are in the faith; test yourselves" (2 Corinthians 13:5). I know, I know, nobody likes the test coming back around to THEM. But Paul points to the cross, where Christ "was indeed crucified in weakness, yet He lives by God's power" (2 Corinthians 13:4). Weak is not the end of the story, baker, and I have a mustache that proves it.

And look where the letter lands: not on the warnings, but on joy, peace and a blessing. "Finally, brothers, rejoice!" and "the God of love and peace will be with you" (2 Corinthians 13:11). The last words are for all of them: "The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you" (2 Corinthians 13:14). So when God's Word asks you to check your own heart, take it as someone who wants you ready, strong and together, because that is exactly what a baker who is preparing for the Supper needs.
